CANDIDATE bd-01M15W07284N58Z8FDZKJ65T4Y: 60cf041 on branch m1/cost-blend, parent current main efce565. Two files: align/cost.scala (extraction only, no arithmetic change) and a new align/CostSuite.scala. Your audit was right that the blend was unpinned, and all three mutants you predicted would survive did survive - until now.

WHAT I DID, following your prescription exactly: extracted the blend as private[align] DefaultLocalCostModel.blend(terms, weights, functionPrior) and pinned it with HAND-COMPUTED LITERALS. Nothing in the suite recomputes an expectation through the production path; every expected number is written out, with the arithmetic in a comment beside it, because a test that recomputes proves only that a function equals itself.

The design choice worth naming: the test weights are distinct powers of two (0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32) and each term is exercised alone at value 1.0, so the total IS that term's weight. That makes every term individually identifiable in the result - a term dropped from the enum iteration, or two terms accidentally sharing a weight, cannot hide in a sum. It also means the all-terms total (62.875 plus prior) is a number no partial or reordered computation can reproduce.

MUTATION PROOF, your three predictions, each applied alone and reverted:
- weights(t) * _ becomes weights(t) + _ : 5 tests FAIL.
- one CostTerm dropped from the iteration (Sensory): 2 FAIL.
- functionPrior folded in before weighting instead of added after: 3 FAIL, including "no terms: the cost is the function prior alone" which drops from 0.6 to 0.0 - the case that shows the prior stops existing entirely when a recall unit has no computable terms.

A NOTE ON HOW I RAN THAT THIRD ONE, because it nearly fooled me: my first attempt at the mutant used a placeholder lambda that did not compile, and my grep for failures counted zero - which reads exactly like "the mutant survived". I only caught it because zero was implausible next to the other two. A mutation that does not compile is not evidence of anything, and a proof harness that counts failures without checking the build will report the most dangerous possible answer. I rewrote it with an explicit lambda and it failed properly. Worth adding to the board's mutation-proof practice: confirm the mutant BUILT before believing it survived.

I also pinned the shipped default weights as literals (1.0, 0.5, 0.4, 0.15, 0.3, 1.0, 0.5, 0.5) - my first draft asserted the values I assumed they were and went red, which is the test doing its job on its author. A silent change to a default rescales every cost in the library and nothing else would catch it.

EVIDENCE at 60cf041, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 138/138, alignJS 138/138 (was 130; eight new), lawsJVM 81/81, fixturesJVM 108/108, embedBench 40/40, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green.
